final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest evescape score (0.934) with strongly favorable structure compatibility (+1.16); charge reversal at a surface-exposed site likely disrupts m102.4-class epitope recognition while preserving folding.
Second-highest escape score (0.906) with the best structure compatibility (+1.28), suggesting strong escape potential without compromising receptor-binding architecture.
High escape score (0.874) and good structural compatibility (0.834); charge reversal should disrupt electrostatic antibody binding while remaining structurally tolerated.

stop_reason.detail: Phenotype and structure evidence converge on a stable top three; remaining tools (MSA, toxin) are unlikely to change the ranking.

history.rationale: Charge reversal in the exposed 408-417 head loop could strongly disrupt m102.4-class recognition while remaining outside the most conserved receptor-pocket core.
Charge-reversal on the exposed head-domain surface is a classic m102.4-class escape mechanism; kept as top candidate pending EVEscape and structure evidence.
Decent escape (0.834) and acceptable structure score (0.680), but outperformed on both axes by the top three.
Removes a polar/asparagine contact in the same solvent-exposed loop and may alter antibody hydrogen bonding with limited structural penalty.
Conservative surface substitution near the putative epitope region; likely tolerated by receptor binding.
Strong escape score (0.880) but moderate structure compatibility (0.641); retained just below the top three.
Introduces a negative charge at a surface-exposed head residue plausibly within neutralizing-antibody reach while preserving local backbone chemistry.
Surface charge change in the receptor-binding head; moderate escape potential with modest structural risk.
Lowest escape score (0.524) among scored candidates; not competitive for the reward.

rejection.reason: Lowest escape score (0.524) among scored candidates; not competitive for the reward.

history.rationale: Local charge inversion near the W390-containing surface patch may reduce antibody affinity more than ephrin binding if this site is antibody-biased.
Strong charge reversal could disrupt the local fold near the ephrin-binding face; slightly down-ranked until structure_compatibility evidence arrives.
Moderate escape (0.776) and structure (0.715); kept as a backup.
A Lys-to-Glu switch on the head-domain surface is a classic escape direction and is distant from cysteines and likely receptor-contact residues.
Charge reversal in the head domain; candidate for epitope disruption, needs EVEscape confirmation.
Weakest structure compatibility in the pool (0.436) signals folding/viability risk despite moderate escape.

rejection.reason: Weakest structure compatibility in the pool (0.436) signals folding/viability risk despite moderate escape.

history.rationale: Charge reversal adjacent to the 421-433 cysteine-rich surface could perturb conformational epitope recognition, with some risk due to nearby disulfide architecture.
Charge reversal with uncertain structural tolerance; lowest-ranked of the pool, kept as backup.
Second-highest escape score (0.906) with the best structure compatibility (+1.28); charge reversal at a surface-exposed site plausibly disrupts antibody binding.
Arginine-to-glutamate in the 441-450 surface region may abolish key antibody salt bridges while retaining a polar side chain for solubility.
Solvent-exposed Arg to Glu could break antibody contacts; kept in pool.
High escape (0.874) with good structural compatibility (0.834); charge reversal should disrupt electrostatic epitope recognition.
Conservative Asp-to-Asn removes a negative charge in the C-terminal head epitope region and can change antibody binding without large steric disruption.
Removes a negative charge that may sit in an antibody contact patch; conservative substitution.
Both phenotype and structure evidence are not applicable (WT mismatch at mapped residue), so it cannot be supported.

rejection.reason: Both phenotype and structure evidence are not applicable (WT mismatch at mapped residue), so it cannot be supported.

history.rationale: Charge reversal in the 481-490 segment may strongly affect m102.4-class binding, though proximity to receptor-binding determinants warrants caution.
Distal surface charge swap, plausibly outside the ephrin-B2/B3 interface; retained pending plausibility checks.
Highest evescape score (0.934) combined with strongly favorable ProteinMPNN delta (+1.16), indicating both escape potential and structural viability.
Glutamine-to-glutamate at a C-terminal head position could alter neutralizing-antibody contacts while keeping residue size and polarity moderate.
Mild surface change; lower expected escape effect but likely safe for receptor binding.
Excellent structure compatibility (0.918) but lower escape score (0.708) limits its priority.
